newsitem.title: INDIA: Toyota's study on Indian venture by June.
newsitem.headline: Toyota's study on Indian venture by June.

text.p: The feasibility study of a possible joint venture between Japan's Toyota Motor Corp and India's Kirloskar group will be ready by June, a Kirloskar official said on Sunday.

"The feasibility report would be ready by June and if all goes well, the project will become operational by 1999," K.K. Swamy, in charge of the feasibility study, told Reuters in Bangalore, capital of the southern state of Karnataka.

The study was commissioned last year to work out the details for a possible joint production project with Toyota and Daihatsu Motor Co, a Toyota affiliate specialising in small cars, and the Kirloskar group.
"We have not yet decided on the model or the size of production. The financial details and the location of the project will be also decided after the feasibility study is over," Swamy said.
Earlier on Friday, Toyota Motor Corp chairman Shoichiro Toyoda, told a news conference in New Delhi that he hoped to meet officials of the Kirloskar group when he went to Bangalore on Monday.
"We are now proceeding with feasibility studies anew," Toyoda said.
Toyoda is leading a business mission of Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren) to India.
Last month Toyota director Hideaki Otaka said the Japanese company was in talks with India's Kirloskar group to form a joint venture car plant in a location still to be decided.
Otaka said Toyota would take a stake of over 50 percent in the planned joint venture.
The Kirloskar official confirmed that Toyota Motor Corp will hold more than 50 percent stake in the proposed project in which Toyota is investing about 30 billion to 50 billion Yen.
